Let
\[
A=(\langle e_i,f_j\rangle),\qquad B=(\langle f_i,g_j\rangle),\qquad C=(\langle g_i,e_j\rangle).
\]
These are orthogonal \(3\times 3\) matrices and
\[
ABC=I.
\]
Also each has constant diagonal. The required quantity is
\[
\left|\prod_{i,j}A_{ij}B_{ij}C_{ij}\right|.
\]

For an orthogonal matrix \(M\) with constant diagonal, replacing \(M\) by \(-M\) if necessary reduces to the case \(M\in SO(3)\), without changing absolute values. Such an \(M\) is a rotation. If its rotation angle is \(\theta\), the equal-diagonal condition forces its rotation axis to have coordinate squares
\[
u_1^2=u_2^2=u_3^2=\frac13.
\]
For such a rotation, after harmless sign changes/permutations, its entries have diagonal value
\[
d=\frac{1+2\cos\theta}{3},
\]
and the product of the three entries in any row has absolute value
\[
D(\theta)=d^2(1-d)
=\frac{2(1+2\cos\theta)^2(1-\cos\theta)}{27}.
\]
Using
\[
1+2\cos\theta=\frac{\sin(3\theta/2)}{\sin(\theta/2)},
\]
this becomes
\[
D(\theta)=\frac{4}{27}\sin^2\frac{3\theta}{2}.
\]
Hence
\[
\prod_{i,j}|M_{ij}|=D(\theta)^3.
\]

It remains to respect \(ABC=I\). If two nonzero-product constant-diagonal rotations have different body-diagonal axes, their quaternion product has vector part whose coordinates cannot again have equal absolute values unless one rotation has \(\theta=0\) or \(\theta=\pm 2\pi/3\), both making \(D(\theta)=0\). Thus at a positive maximum all three rotations share the same axis, so their angles \(\theta_1,\theta_2,\theta_3\) satisfy
\[
\theta_1+\theta_2+\theta_3\equiv 0\pmod{2\pi}.
\]
Therefore
\[
\prod_{\ell=1}^3D(\theta_\ell)
=\left(\frac4{27}\right)^3
\prod_{\ell=1}^3\sin^2\frac{3\theta_\ell}{2}.
\]
Let \(x_\ell=\frac{3\theta_\ell}{2}\). Then \(x_1+x_2+x_3\equiv0\pmod{3\pi}\), and
\[
|\sin x_1\sin x_2\sin x_3|\le \left(\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\right)^3.
\]
So
\[
\prod_{\ell=1}^3D(\theta_\ell)
\le
\left(\frac4{27}\right)^3\left(\frac{27}{64}\right)
=\frac1{729}.
\]
Thus the original product is at most
\[
\left(\frac1{729}\right)^3=\frac1{3^{18}}.
\]

Equality is attained by taking all three rotations about the same body-diagonal axis, for example with angles
\[
\theta_1=\theta_2=\frac{4\pi}{9},\qquad \theta_3=\frac{10\pi}{9},
\]
whose sum is \(2\pi\), so \(ABC=I\), and each satisfies
\[
\sin^2\frac{3\theta_\ell}{2}=\frac34.
\]

\[
\boxed{\frac1{3^{18}}}
\]
